# Demographic Summary

```{r}
#| echo: false

d1 <- rename_values(d1)

freq_table <- function(x, var_label) {
  tbl <- sort(table(x, useNA = "ifany"), decreasing = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    Variable = c(var_label, rep("", length(tbl) - 1)),
    Level    = names(tbl),
    N        = as.integer(tbl),
    `%`      = paste0(round(100 * as.integer(tbl) / sum(tbl), 1), "%"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

freq_table_multi <- function(x, var_label) {
  n_participants <- sum(!is.na(x))
  all_labels <- unlist(strsplit(na.omit(as.character(x)), " / "))
  tbl        <- sort(table(all_labels), decreasing = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    Variable = c(var_label, rep("", length(tbl) - 1)),
    Level    = names(tbl),
    N        = as.integer(tbl),
    `%`      = paste0(round(100 * as.integer(tbl) / n_participants, 1), "%"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

# Exploratory Factor Analysis

In this section, we explore the dimensionality of the Michele instrument. First, the data is cleaned to only contain the Michele instrument responses. Then KMO and Bartlett's tests are used to understand if the data is suitable for factor analysis. Second, the EFA is run for the cleaned data. Parallel analysis is used to understand how many factors are estimated to be in the data by simulating factor analyses. The number of factors for the actual EFA analysis is determined by this parallel simulation.

## Prepping the data for EFA

Here, data is cleaned from the long format and to remove other varibles than those in the Michele instrument. The KMO is good overall (.85) and for the individual items (range = .78-.92). The Bartlett's test (χ2(66) = 1447.01, p < .001) indicated items had sufficient correlations for factor analysis processes.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: prep_EFA

# We need temporarily remove the other instruments from the data frame because we only care about Michele's instrument for the EFA.

d1_long_clean <- prepare_EFA(d1_long, instrument_name = "Michele")

cm <- cor(d1_long_clean, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
KMO(cm)
cortest.bartlett(cm, n = nrow(d1_long_clean))

```

## Running an EFA

Before performing an EFA, parallel analysis was used to determine the number of factors to retain. This determined that a three factor solution best fit the data, following the simulations (shown on Scree Plots).

Factor analysis was then conducted on the 12 item Michele instrument using a Maximum Likelihood method (ML) with an oblimin rotation. Considering the sample size (> 200) ML was used to further investigate the statistical significance of the obtained factor loadings (Hair et al., 2019). An oblique rotation method was employed because it is assumed that factors will be correlated (Tabachnick & Fidell, 2019).

Together, the three factors explain 64% of the variance. Factor 1 explains 23% of the variance (4 items), as does Factor 2 (4 items). Factor 3 explains 18% of the total variance (4 items). The communalities of the items, however, ranged from .389 (Q20_5) to .844 (Q20_10) (M = .64). One item (Q20_5) had a communality below the recommended threshold of .40 (.389; Costello & Osborne, 2005) and another item (Q20_6) cross-loaded on Factor 1. Q20_6 was removed and the EFA repeated; Q20_5 was retained because its communality rose above .40 in the 11-item solution.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: michele_EFA
set.seed(3108)

# obtaining communality descriptions
comm_table <- function(x) list(
  Mean = mean(x$communality),
  Median = median(x$communality),
  Range = range(x$communality))

# EFA simulation
output <- fa.parallel(d1_long_clean, fm = "ml",sim = FALSE)

# running EFA with the retained simulated factor structure (3 factors) 
fa_sol_d1_long_clean <- fa(d1_long_clean, nfactors = output$nfact, n.iter = 0, 
                  rotate = "oblimin", missing = TRUE, warnings = TRUE, 
                  fm = "ml")

print(fa_sol_d1_long_clean)
print(fa_sol_d1_long_clean$loadings, cutoff = 0.2)

print(fa_sol_d1_long_clean$communality)
comm_table(fa_sol_d1_long_clean)

psych::alpha(d1_long_clean)

# Q20_5 has poor communality which hinders the factor loading. Q20_6 had a cross-loading with the first factor so should also be removed. The rest of the items are quite good (> .40)

d1_long_clean2 <- dplyr::select(d1_long_clean, -Q20_6)

output <- fa.parallel(d1_long_clean2, fm = "ml",sim = FALSE)

fa_sol_d1_long_clean2 <- fa(d1_long_clean2, nfactors = output$nfact, n.iter = 0, 
                  rotate = "oblimin", missing = TRUE, warnings = TRUE, 
                  fm = "ml")

print(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2)
print(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$loadings, cutoff = 0.2)

print(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$communality)
comm_table(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2)


psych::alpha(d1_long_clean2)

# There are three factors with strong items in each factor. While removing the two low communiality items improves the factors, future issues for confirmatory analyses will be impacted by only having 2 indicators for the second factor. 

```

## Scoring keys and consistency checks

The final LoiTeS has 11 items (Q20_6 was removed). All scores used downstream (correlations, regressions) are built from the keys defined here so that the removed item can never re-enter a total or subscale score. The chunk also checks (a) that no retained item is negatively keyed in the raw data (i.e., that no reverse-scoring is needed), (b) that the subscale keys match the primary loadings of the final EFA, and (c) defines the OSTES subscale key.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: scoring_keys

# ---- LoiTeS final key (11 items) ----------------------------------------
loites_removed <- "Q20_6"

loites_subscales <- list(
  F1_Colleagues = c("Q20_1", "Q20_2", "Q20_3", "Q20_4"),
  F2_Belonging  = c("Q20_9", "Q20_10", "Q20_11", "Q20_12"),
  F3_Students   = c("Q20_5", "Q20_7", "Q20_8")
)
loites_items <- unlist(loites_subscales, use.names = FALSE)
sub_of_item  <- setNames(rep(names(loites_subscales), lengths(loites_subscales)),
                         loites_items)

stopifnot(length(loites_items) == 11,
          !(loites_removed %in% loites_items),
          all(loites_items %in% names(d1_long_clean2)))

# ---- OSTES short-form key -------------------------------------------------
#short-form key (Tschannen-Moran & Woolfolk Hoy) # Verify items are the same... (seems to be so!)
ostes_key_published <- list(
  instruction   = c("Q24_5", "Q24_9", "Q24_10", "Q24_12"),
  class_manager = c("Q24_1", "Q24_6", "Q24_7", "Q24_8"),
  engagement    = c("Q24_2", "Q24_3", "Q24_4", "Q24_11")
)
# Key used in the earlier version of this script
ostes_key_previous <- list(
  instruction   = c("Q24_5", "Q24_9", "Q24_10", "Q24_12"),
  class_manager = c("Q24_1", "Q24_3", "Q24_6", "Q24_8"),
  engagement    = c("Q24_2", "Q24_4", "Q24_7", "Q24_11")
)
ostes_key <- ostes_key_published
stopifnot(setequal(unlist(ostes_key), paste0("Q24_", 1:12)))

# ---- Strict summed score: NA if any item is missing (WHO-5, R-UCLA) -------
row_sum_strict <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  ifelse(rowSums(is.na(x)) > 0, NA_real_, rowSums(x))
}

# ---- Check 1: response range and item direction (raw, wide data) ----------
raw_loites <- d1 %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c(loites_items, loites_removed))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

cat("Observed response range (expect 1-5):", range(raw_loites, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

r_raw <- cor(raw_loites, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cat("Lowest inter-item r among the 11 retained items:",
    round(min(r_raw[loites_items, loites_items]), 2), "\n")
cat("Correlations of the removed item (Q20_6) with the retained items:\n")
print(round(r_raw[loites_removed, loites_items], 2))

if (any(r_raw[loites_items, loites_items] < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  warning("A retained LoiTeS item correlates negatively with another: check whether reverse-scoring is needed.")
}
if (mean(r_raw[loites_removed, loites_items], na.rm = TRUE) < 0) {
  message("Q20_6 correlates negatively with the retained items: it appears to be negatively keyed ",
          "(and was not reverse-scored in the raw data).")
}

# ---- Check 2: do the subscale keys match the primary loadings of the EFA? --
L <- unclass(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$loadings)
primary_factor <- apply(abs(L), 1, which.max)

loadings_check <- data.frame(
  item     = rownames(L),
  subscale = sub_of_item[rownames(L)],
  primary  = colnames(L)[primary_factor],
  loading  = round(L[cbind(seq_len(nrow(L)), primary_factor)], 2),
  row.names = NULL
)

keys_match_efa <-
  all(tapply(loadings_check$primary, loadings_check$subscale,
             function(x) length(unique(x)) == 1)) &&
  length(unique(loadings_check$primary)) == length(loites_subscales)

if (!keys_match_efa) {
  warning("Subscale keys do not match the primary loadings of the final EFA: revise loites_subscales.")
}

factor_map <- sapply(loites_subscales, function(v) colnames(L)[primary_factor[v[1]]])

loadings_check
factor_map
```

## Item distributions and the matrix analysed

Maximum likelihood on Pearson correlations is defensible for 7-category items only if the item distributions are not too irregular. This chunk reports, for each retained item, mean, SD, skewness, excess kurtosis, floor and ceiling percentages (% of responses at 1 and 5), and missing responses. Items with skew >= 2 or excess kurtosis >= 5 are flagged for "severe" non-normality. Multivariate skewness and kurtosis are also reported.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: item_distributions

# Items of the final 11-item scale, as analysed in the final EFA
d_items <- dplyr::select(d1_long_clean2, all_of(loites_items)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

item_desc <- as.data.frame(psych::describe(d_items))[
  , c("n", "mean", "sd", "median", "min", "max", "skew", "kurtosis")]
item_desc$pct_floor   <- sapply(d_items, function(x) 100 * mean(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
item_desc$pct_ceiling <- sapply(d_items, function(x) 100 * mean(x == 5, na.rm = TRUE))
item_desc$n_missing   <- colSums(is.na(d_items))
item_desc$flag        <- ifelse(abs(item_desc$skew) >= 2 | abs(item_desc$kurtosis) >= 5,
                                "check", "")
item_desc <- data.frame(item = rownames(item_desc), item_desc, row.names = NULL)

kableExtra::kbl(
  item_desc,
  caption  = "LoiTeS item descriptives and distribution diagnostics (11 retained items)",
  booktabs = TRUE,
  digits   = 2
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("scale_down", "hold_position"), font_size = 10) %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general = "Skew and kurtosis from psych::describe (kurtosis = excess). Floor/ceiling = % of responses at 1 / 5.",
    general_title = "Note.", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

This chunk documents how much data are missing and how missingness is handled, and checks whether the EFA is sensitive to it.

```{r}

#| id: missing_data

# LoiTeS (11 items)
miss_loites <- data.frame(
  N_respondents     = nrow(d_items),
  N_complete        = sum(complete.cases(d_items)),
  N_any_missing     = sum(!complete.cases(d_items)),
  pct_cells_missing = round(100 * mean(is.na(as.matrix(d_items))), 2)
)
miss_loites

# All instruments in the wide data: respondents with at least one missing item
miss_instruments <- data.frame(
  instrument   = names(instruments),
  n_items      = lengths(instruments),
  n_incomplete = sapply(instruments, function(v) sum(!complete.cases(d1[, v]))),
  row.names = NULL
)
miss_instruments

# Sensitivity: complete-case EFA vs. the (median-imputed) EFA used in the paper
if (miss_loites$N_any_missing > 0) {
  fa_cc <- fa(na.omit(d_items), nfactors = 3, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "ml")
  cat("Tucker congruence, complete-case vs. imputed solution:\n")
  print(round(psych::factor.congruence(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2, fa_cc), 2))
} else {
  cat("No missing LoiTeS responses: imputed and complete-case solutions are identical.\n")
}

# Scoring rules used in score_df (see correlations section):
#  - LoiTeS, OSTES, MSPSS: mean of available items (na.rm = TRUE)
#  - WHO-5, R-UCLA: strict sums (NA if any item missing); WHO-5 x 4 = 0-100
```

## Sensitivity analysis with polychoric correlations

The 5-category items are re-analysed with polychoric correlations and MINRES extraction (oblimin rotation, three factors). Parallel analysis is repeated on the polychoric matrix. The solution is compared with the ML/Pearson solution by Tucker congruence, loading-by-loading, and by the proportion of items with the same primary factor.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: polychoric_sensitivity
set.seed(3108)

# Parallel analysis on the polychoric matrix
pa_poly <- fa.parallel(d_items, fm = "minres", fa = "fa", cor = "poly", sim = FALSE)
cat("Factors suggested by polychoric parallel analysis:", pa_poly$nfact, "\n")

# Three-factor EFA, polychoric correlations, MINRES, oblimin
fa_poly <- fa(d_items, nfactors = 3, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "minres", cor = "poly")
print(fa_poly$loadings, cutoff = 0.2)

# Compare with the ML / Pearson solution (fa_sol_d1_long_clean2)
cong       <- psych::factor.congruence(L, unclass(fa_poly$loadings)[rownames(L), ])
poly_match <- apply(abs(cong), 1, which.max)             # poly factor matching each ML factor
poly_sign  <- sign(cong[cbind(seq_len(nrow(cong)), poly_match)])
cat("Tucker congruence (rows = ML/Pearson, columns = MINRES/polychoric):\n")
print(round(cong, 2))

Lp <- unclass(fa_poly$loadings)[, poly_match, drop = FALSE]
Lp <- sweep(Lp, 2, poly_sign, "*")                       # align order and sign

poly_compare <- data.frame(
  item        = rownames(L),
  subscale    = sub_of_item[rownames(L)],
  ML_pearson  = round(L[cbind(seq_len(nrow(L)), primary_factor)], 2),
  MINRES_poly = round(Lp[cbind(seq_len(nrow(Lp)), primary_factor)], 2),
  row.names = NULL
)

prim_poly  <- apply(abs(unclass(fa_poly$loadings)), 1, which.max)
ml_equiv   <- sapply(prim_poly, function(q) which(poly_match == q)[1])
same_assign <- mean(ml_equiv == primary_factor, na.rm = TRUE)

poly_fit <- data.frame(
  Solution = c("ML / Pearson", "MINRES / polychoric"),
  TLI      = c(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$TLI,    fa_poly$TLI),
  RMSEA    = c(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$RMSEA[1], fa_poly$RMSEA[1]),
  RMSR     = c(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$rms,    fa_poly$rms)
)

cat("Proportion of items with the same primary factor in both solutions:",
    round(same_assign, 2), "\n")
poly_compare
poly_fit
```

## Reliability by subscale

Cronbach's alpha (with Feldt 95% CIs), McDonald's omega (one-factor model within each subscale; percentile bootstrap 95% CIs), corrected item-total correlations computed within each subscale, and correlations between the three factors with 95% CIs. Latent factor correlations are bootstrapped with factors aligned to the reference solution by Tucker congruence; observed subscale-score correlations are reported as well.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: subscale_reliability
set.seed(3108)

feldt_ci <- function(alpha, n, k, level = .95) {
  a   <- (1 - level) / 2
  df1 <- n - 1
  df2 <- (n - 1) * (k - 1)
  c(lower = 1 - (1 - alpha) * qf(1 - a, df1, df2),
    upper = 1 - (1 - alpha) * qf(a,     df1, df2))
}

# Standardised one-factor omega
omega_1f <- function(x) {
  f   <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(psych::fa(x, nfactors = 1, fm = "ml")))
  lam <- as.numeric(f$loadings)
  lam <- lam * sign(sum(lam))
  sum(lam)^2 / (sum(lam)^2 + sum(1 - lam^2))
}

boot_omega <- function(x, B = 1000) {
  x   <- x[complete.cases(x), , drop = FALSE]
  est <- omega_1f(x)
  bs  <- replicate(B, tryCatch(omega_1f(x[sample(nrow(x), replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]),
                               error = function(e) NA_real_))
  c(omega = est,
    lower = unname(quantile(bs, .025, na.rm = TRUE)),
    upper = unname(quantile(bs, .975, na.rm = TRUE)),
    boot_failed = sum(is.na(bs)))
}

rel_rows <- list(); item_rows <- list()
for (s in names(loites_subscales)) {
  x   <- d_items[, loites_subscales[[s]], drop = FALSE]
  a   <- psych::alpha(x, check.keys = FALSE)
  n_s <- sum(complete.cases(x))
  k_s <- ncol(x)
  ci  <- feldt_ci(a$total$raw_alpha, n_s, k_s)
  om  <- boot_omega(x)

  rel_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(
    Subscale = s, k = k_s, N = n_s,
    alpha = a$total$raw_alpha, alpha_low = ci["lower"], alpha_high = ci["upper"],
    omega = om["omega"], omega_low = om["lower"], omega_high = om["upper"],
    mean_inter_item_r = a$total$average_r,
    row.names = NULL
  )
  item_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(
    Subscale = s, item = rownames(a$item.stats),
    r_item_total_corrected = a$item.stats$r.drop,
    alpha_if_dropped = a$alpha.drop$raw_alpha,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
rel_tab  <- do.call(rbind, rel_rows)
item_tab <- do.call(rbind, item_rows)

kableExtra::kbl(rel_tab, caption = "Subscale reliability (alpha: Feldt 95% CI; omega: bootstrap 95% CI)",
                booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("scale_down", "hold_position"), font_size = 10)

kableExtra::kbl(item_tab, caption = "Corrected item-total correlations within subscales",
                booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 10)

# ---- Correlations between the factors ------------------------------------
# (a) latent factor correlations from the oblimin EFA, bootstrap CIs
boot_phi <- function(data, ref, B = 500) {
  k   <- ncol(ref$loadings)
  out <- array(NA_real_, c(B, k, k))
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    d_b <- data[sample(nrow(data), replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
    f_b <- tryCatch(
      suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
        fa(d_b, nfactors = k, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "ml", missing = TRUE))),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(f_b)) next
    cg  <- psych::factor.congruence(ref, f_b)
    ord <- apply(abs(cg), 1, which.max)
    if (anyDuplicated(ord)) next
    sgn <- sign(cg[cbind(seq_len(k), ord)])
    out[b, , ] <- f_b$Phi[ord, ord] * (sgn %o% sgn)
  }
  out
}

phi_boot <- boot_phi(d1_long_clean2[, rownames(fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$loadings)],
fa_sol_d1_long_clean2)
pairs    <- combn(seq_along(loites_subscales), 2)
phi_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(pairs)), function(j) {
  i1 <- match(factor_map[pairs[1, j]], colnames(L))
  i2 <- match(factor_map[pairs[2, j]], colnames(L))
  
  # vector of bootstrapped correlations
  vec <- phi_boot[, i1, i2]
  
  # Count valid (non-NA) results
  valid_count <- sum(!is.na(vec))
  
  if (valid_count == 0) {
    # check if we can calculate CI
    return(data.frame(
      Pair = paste(names(loites_subscales)[pairs[1, j]], "-", names(loites_subscales)[pairs[2, j]]),
      phi = NA,
      lower = NA,
      upper = NA
    ))
  }
  
  # Quantile Calculation
  lower_raw <- quantile(vec, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  upper_raw <- quantile(vec, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # if quantile fails or returns weird results
  lower <- min(lower_raw, upper_raw)
  upper <- max(lower_raw, upper_raw)
  
  data.frame(
    Pair = paste(names(loites_subscales)[pairs[1, j]], "-", names(loites_subscales)[pairs[2, j]]),
    phi = fa_sol_d1_long_clean2$Phi[i1, i2],
    lower = lower,
    upper = upper
  )
}))

# (b) observed subscale-score correlations with 95% CIs
sub_scores <- as.data.frame(sapply(loites_subscales,
                                   function(v) rowMeans(d_items[, v, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)))
sub_cor <- psych::corr.test(sub_scores, adjust = "none")

kableExtra::kbl(phi_tab, caption = "Latent factor correlations (oblimin EFA; bootstrap 95% CI)",
                booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 10)

kableExtra::kbl(sub_cor$ci[, c("lower", "r", "upper", "p")],
                caption = "Observed subscale-score correlations (Pearson, 95% CI)",
                booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 10)
```

## Omega hierarchical

A Schmid-Leiman bifactor-type decomposition of the three-factor solution gives omega total (ω_t), omega hierarchical (ω_h; variance due to the general factor), omega for each group factor, and the explained common variance (ECV). Bootstrap CIs are provided for ω_h and ω_t. These estimates are exploratory (EFA-based, N = 211) and should be confirmed with a CFA bifactor comparison with later data.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| id: omega_hierarchical
set.seed(3108)

om <- psych::omega(d_items, nfactors = 3, fm = "ml", rotate = "oblimin",
                   plot = FALSE)

# Explained common variance (general factor vs. group factors)
sl       <- om$schmid$sl
g_load   <- sl[, "g"]
grp_load <- sl[, grep("\\*$", colnames(sl)), drop = FALSE]
ecv      <- sum(g_load^2) / (sum(g_load^2) + sum(grp_load^2))

boot_om <- replicate(500, tryCatch({
  b <- d_items[sample(nrow(d_items), replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  o <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    psych::omega(b, nfactors = 3, fm = "ml", plot = FALSE)))
  c(omega_h = o$omega_h, omega_t = o$omega.tot)
}, error = function(e) c(omega_h = NA_real_, omega_t = NA_real_)))

omega_tab <- data.frame(
  Index    = c("omega_total", "omega_hierarchical", "omega_h / omega_total", "ECV"),
  Estimate = c(om$omega.tot, om$omega_h, om$omega_h / om$omega.tot, ecv),
  CI_low   = c(quantile(boot_om["omega_t", ], .025, na.rm = TRUE),
               quantile(boot_om["omega_h", ], .025, na.rm = TRUE), NA, NA),
  CI_high  = c(quantile(boot_om["omega_t", ], .975, na.rm = TRUE),
               quantile(boot_om["omega_h", ], .975, na.rm = TRUE), NA, NA)
)

kableExtra::kbl(omega_tab, caption = "Omega coefficients for the 11-item, three-factor solution",
                booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 10)

# Omega for the general and group factors separately
kableExtra::kbl(om$omega.group, caption = "Omega by general / group factor (rotated factors F1*-F3*)",
                booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 10)
```

```{r}

# make sure everything is numeric!
d1_cor <- d1 %>% mutate(across(matches("^Q(20|22|24|26|28)_"), as.numeric))

# Need to calculate the scores for the instruments prior to correlation

score_df <- d1_cor %>%
  mutate(

    WHO5_total = row_sum_strict(

    Michele_full  = rowMeans(across(all_of(loites_items)), na.rm = TRUE),

    Hughes_total  = row_sum_strict(across(all_of(paste0('Q22_', 1:20)))),

# Display: correlation table with significance stars
add_stars <- function(r_mat, p_mat) {
  stars <- ifelse(p_mat < .001, "***",
           ifelse(p_mat < .010, "**",
           ifelse(p_mat < .050, "*", "")))
  matrix(
    paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r_mat), stars),
    nrow  = nrow(r_mat),
    dimnames = dimnames(r_mat)
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| id: ref_coding

# Coding of categorical predictors -------------------------------------------
# A tiny reference group (e.g. fixed-term teachers) makes every coefficient unstable, so:
#   1. pool very small categories (n < min_n) 
#   2. use the LARGEST remaining category as the reference

collapse_rare <- function(x, min_n = 10, label = "Other") {
  x  <- as.character(x)
  tb <- table(x)
  x[x %in% names(tb)[tb < min_n]] <- label
  x
}

set_ref <- function(x) {
  x <- factor(x)
  relevel(x, ref = names(which.max(table(x))))
}

score_df <- score_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Gender     = set_ref(Gender),
    EmpStatus  = set_ref(collapse_rare(EmpStatus,  label = "Other")),
    OftenTeach = set_ref(collapse_rare(OftenTeach, label = "Other / infrequent")),
    Qualified  = set_ref(collapse_rare(Qualified,  label = "Other")),
    Formal     = set_ref(Formal)
  )

# YearTaught is an ordered grouping: reference = shortest experience
score_df$YearTaught <- relevel(factor(score_df$YearTaught), ref = "1-7 years")

# Table of reference groups (goes in the Supplementary Material)
cat_vars <- c("Gender", "YearTaught", "EmpStatus", "OftenTeach", "Qualified", "Formal")

ref_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cat_vars, function(v) {
  x   <- score_df[[v]]
  lev <- levels(x)
  tb  <- table(x)
  data.frame(
    Variable        = v,
    Reference       = lev[1],
    N_reference     = as.integer(tb[1]),
    `Compared levels (n)` = paste0(lev[-1], " (", as.integer(tb[-1]), ")", collapse = "; "),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

kableExtra::kbl(ref_table, caption = "Reference groups for categorical predictors",
                booktabs = TRUE) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "striped"),
                            full_width = TRUE)
```

# Regression Models 

Want to compare how the variables for the teacher demographics relate to the responses to the WHO-5, LoiTeS, Hughes, Tschannen, and Zimet instruments. Ignoring the country here as the N=211 could not suit as a comparision across culture or country.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| id: mixed_Models

# Expand multi-select columns 
expand_multiselect <- function(df, col) {
  all_opts <- df[[col]] |>
    na.omit() |>
    strsplit(" / ") |>
    unlist() |>
    trimws() |>
    unique() |>
    sort()

  for (opt in all_opts) {
    new_col <- paste0(col, "_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", opt))
    df[[new_col]] <- as.integer(
      !is.na(df[[col]]) & grepl(opt, df[[col]], fixed = TRUE)
    )
  }
  df
}

score_df <- expand_multiselect(score_df, "TeachAct")
score_df <- expand_multiselect(score_df, "Role")
score_df <- expand_multiselect(score_df, "LvlTaught")

# Predictors
demo_scalar    <- c("Age", "Gender", "YearTaught", "EmpStatus",
                    "OftenTeach", "Qualified", "Formal")

demo_TeachAct  <- grep("^TeachAct_",  names(score_df), value = TRUE)
demo_Role      <- grep("^Role_",      names(score_df), value = TRUE)
demo_LvlTaught <- grep("^LvlTaught_", names(score_df), value = TRUE)

demo_vars   <- c(demo_scalar, demo_TeachAct, demo_Role, demo_LvlTaught)
focused_rhs <- paste(c(demo_scalar, demo_TeachAct), collapse = " + ")

# Analysis
use_mixed <- FALSE   # TRUE → lmer() + (1|EmpCount);  FALSE → lm()

fit_model <- function(outcome, rhs, mixed = use_mixed) {
  fml <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", rhs))
  if (mixed) {
    fml_mixed <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", rhs, "+ (1 | EmpCount)"))
    lmer(fml_mixed, data = score_df, REML = FALSE,
         control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  } else {
    lm(fml, data = score_df)
  }
}

extract_fixed <- function(model, outcome_name) {
  if (inherits(model, "lmerMod")) {
    coef_table <- coef(summary(model))
    ci         <- confint(model, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
  } else {
    coef_table <- coef(summary(model))
    ci         <- confint(model)
  }
  data.frame(
    outcome   = outcome_name,
    term      = rownames(coef_table),
    estimate  = coef_table[, "Estimate"],
    std.error = coef_table[, "Std. Error"],
    statistic = coef_table[, "t value"],
    p.value   = coef_table[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    conf.low  = ci[rownames(coef_table), 1],
    conf.high = ci[rownames(coef_table), 2],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

# Broad sweep 
outcomes <- c(
  "WHO5_total",
  "Michele_full", "Michele_F1", "Michele_F2", "Michele_F3",
  "Hughes_total",
  "Tschannen_total", "Tschannen_instruction",
  "Tschannen_class_manager", "Tschannen_engagement",
  "Zimet_total", "Zimet_sig_other", "Zimet_family", "Zimet_friends"
)

broad_models <- lapply(setNames(outcomes, outcomes), function(outcome) {
  fit_model(outcome, paste(demo_vars, collapse = " + "))
})

broad_tidy <- bind_rows(
  mapply(extract_fixed,
         model        = broad_models,
         outcome_name = names(broad_models),
         SIMPLIFY     = FALSE)
)

sig_predictors <- broad_tidy |>
  filter(p.value < .05, term != "(Intercept)") |>
  dplyr::select(outcome, term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) |>
  arrange(outcome, p.value)

print(sig_predictors)

# ICC (mixed models only) 
if (use_mixed) {
  icc_vals <- sapply(broad_models, function(m) {
    vc          <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
    country_var <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "EmpCount"]
    resid_var   <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]
    country_var / (country_var + resid_var)
  })
  print(round(icc_vals, 3))
}

# Focused models 

# WHO-5
m_WHO5_cross <- fit_model("WHO5_total", focused_rhs)
summary(m_WHO5_cross)

# LoiTeS full + sub-scales
m_LoiTeS_full <- fit_model("Michele_full", focused_rhs)
m_LoiTeS_F1   <- fit_model("Michele_F1",   focused_rhs)
m_LoiTeS_F2   <- fit_model("Michele_F2",   focused_rhs)
m_LoiTeS_F3   <- fit_model("Michele_F3",   focused_rhs)
summary(m_LoiTeS_full)

# Hughes
m_Hughes <- fit_model("Hughes_total", focused_rhs)
summary(m_Hughes)

# Tschannen-Moran
m_Tschannen_total <- fit_model("Tschannen_total",         focused_rhs)
m_Tschannen_instr <- fit_model("Tschannen_instruction",   focused_rhs)
m_Tschannen_mgmt  <- fit_model("Tschannen_class_manager", focused_rhs)
m_Tschannen_eng   <- fit_model("Tschannen_engagement",    focused_rhs)
summary(m_Tschannen_total)

# Zimet MSPSS
m_Zimet_total <- fit_model("Zimet_total",     focused_rhs)
m_Zimet_sig   <- fit_model("Zimet_sig_other", focused_rhs)
m_Zimet_fam   <- fit_model("Zimet_family",    focused_rhs)
m_Zimet_frd   <- fit_model("Zimet_friends",   focused_rhs)
summary(m_Zimet_total)

# Cross-instrument model
cross_rhs <- paste(
  c("Tschannen_total", "Zimet_total", "WHO5_total",
    "Age", "Gender", "YearTaught", "EmpStatus"),
  collapse = " + "
)
m_LoiTeS_cross <- fit_model("Michele_full", cross_rhs)
summary(m_LoiTeS_cross)

# Model comparison
m_LoiTeS_noGender <- fit_model(
  "Michele_full",
  paste(setdiff(c(demo_scalar, demo_TeachAct), "Gender"), collapse = " + ")
)
anova(m_LoiTeS_noGender, m_LoiTeS_full)

# plots
plot_coefs <- function(model, title = "") {
  coef_df <- extract_fixed(model, outcome_name = "")
  coef_df |>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(term, estimate))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                   height = 0.2, colour = "steelblue") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "steelblue") +
    labs(title = title, x = "Estimate (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)
}

plot_coefs(m_LoiTeS_full,     "LoiTeS")
plot_coefs(m_WHO5_cross,      "WHO-5")
plot_coefs(m_Hughes,          "Hughes")
plot_coefs(m_Tschannen_total, "Tschannen")
plot_coefs(m_Zimet_total,     "Zimet")
```

## Functions for making comparisons

VIF/tolerance, residual diagnostics, homoscedasticity, influential cases, confidence intervals, and determining reference groups

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| id: reg_helpers

# Robust HC3 (small-sample heteroscedasticity-consistent) coefficients with 95% CIs 

robust_coefs <- function(model, type = "HC3") {
  vc  <- sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = type)
  dfr <- df.residual(model)
  ct  <- lmtest::coeftest(model, vcov. = vc, df = dfr)
  ci  <- lmtest::coefci(model,   vcov. = vc, df = dfr, level = .95)
  data.frame(
    Term      = rownames(ct),
    B         = ct[, 1],
    SE_robust = ct[, 2],
    CI_low    = ci[, 1],
    CI_high   = ci[, 2],
    p         = ct[, 4],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

# VIF / tolerance ---------------------------------------------------------------
# car::vif() returns GVIF for factors; GVIF^(1/(2*Df)) squared is comparable to a
# usual VIF. Tolerance = 1 / VIF.
vif_table <- function(model) {
  v <- car::vif(model)
  if (is.matrix(v)) {
    out <- data.frame(Predictor = rownames(v), Df = v[, "Df"],
                      VIF = v[, "GVIF^(1/(2*Df))"]^2, row.names = NULL)
  } else {
    out <- data.frame(Predictor = names(v), Df = 1, VIF = as.numeric(v))
  }
  out$Tolerance <- 1 / out$VIF
  out
}

# One-row diagnostic summary per model ----------------------------------------
diagnose_lm <- function(model, label) {
  n  <- nobs(model)
  k  <- length(coef(model)) - 1
  v  <- tryCatch({
    vv <- car::vif(model)
    if (is.matrix(vv)) vv[, "GVIF^(1/(2*Df))"]^2 else vv
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
  cd <- cooks.distance(model)
  data.frame(
    Model        = label,
    N            = n,
    Predictors   = k,
    Max_VIF      = round(suppressWarnings(max(v, na.rm = TRUE)), 2),
    BP_p         = signif(lmtest::bptest(model)$p.value, 3),     # homoscedasticity
    Shapiro_p    = signif(shapiro.test(residuals(model))$p.value, 3),  # residual normality
    N_Cook       = sum(cd > 4 / n),                              # influential cases
    N_leverage   = sum(hatvalues(model) > 3 * (k + 1) / n),      # high leverage
    N_stdres_gt3 = sum(abs(rstandard(model)) > 3)                # outliers
  )
}
```

# Hierarchical regression: does LoiTeS retain associations after accounting for general loneliness?

LoiTeS total score was regressed on R-UCLA loneliness plus theoretically motivated
controls (Block 1), and then on MSPSS, WHO-5 and OSTES (Block 2). Cases are
restricted to complete data on all variables so ΔR² is computed on the same sample.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| id: hierarchical

hier_df <- score_df %>%
  dplyr::select(Michele_full, Hughes_total, Age, Gender, YearTaught, EmpStatus,
                Zimet_total, WHO5_total, Tschannen_total) %>%
  dplyr::filter(complete.cases(.)) %>%
  droplevels()

cat("Complete cases in hierarchical models: N =", nrow(hier_df), "\n")

# 1: general loneliness + controls
m_h1 <- lm(Michele_full ~ Hughes_total + Age + Gender + YearTaught + EmpStatus,
           data = hier_df)
summary(m_h1)

# 2: + support (MSPSS), wellbeing (WHO-5), self-efficacy (OSTES)
m_h2 <- lm(Michele_full ~ Hughes_total + Age + Gender + YearTaught + EmpStatus +
             Zimet_total + WHO5_total + Tschannen_total,
           data = hier_df)
summary(m_h2)

hier_models <- list("1: R-UCLA + controls"       = m_h1,
                    "2: + MSPSS, WHO-5, OSTES"   = m_h2)

# R2, adjusted R2, change in R2
hier_fit <- data.frame(
  Model  = names(hier_models),
  R2     = sapply(hier_models, function(m) summary(m)$r.squared),
  Adj_R2 = sapply(hier_models, function(m) summary(m)$adj.r.squared),
  row.names = NULL
)
hier_fit$Delta_R2 <- c(NA, diff(hier_fit$R2))

# Test of the change in R2: classical F and heteroscedasticity-robust (HC3) Wald F
chg_classic <- anova(m_h1, m_h2)
chg_robust  <- lmtest::waldtest(m_h1, m_h2,
                                vcov = function(x) sandwich::vcovHC(x, type = "HC3"))

hier_change <- data.frame(
  Test = c("F change (classical)", "F change (HC3 robust)"),
  F    = c(chg_classic$F[2], chg_robust$F[2]),
  df1  = c(abs(chg_classic$Df[2]), abs(chg_robust$Df[2])),
  df2  = c(chg_classic$Res.Df[2], chg_robust$Res.Df[2]),
  p    = c(chg_classic$`Pr(>F)`[2], chg_robust$`Pr(>F)`[2])
)

kableExtra::kbl(hier_fit,    digits = 3, caption = "Hierarchical models: R2 and change in R2") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
kableExtra::kbl(hier_change, digits = 3, caption = "Test of the change in R2 (2 over 1)") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

# Coefficients with robust SEs and 95% CIs (reference groups: see ref_table)
kableExtra::kbl(robust_coefs(m_h1), digits = 3,
                caption = "1: coefficients with HC3 robust SEs and 95% CIs") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
kableExtra::kbl(robust_coefs(m_h2), digits = 3,
                caption = "2: coefficients with HC3 robust SEs and 95% CIs") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

# Multicollinearity
kableExtra::kbl(vif_table(m_h2), digits = 2,
                caption = "2: VIF and tolerance (GVIF-adjusted for categorical terms)") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

#| id: reporting_tables

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p))))

# ---- Table 1: omnibus fit of every demographic model -----------------------------
omnibus_row <- function(model, label) {
  s <- summary(model)
  f <- s$fstatistic
  data.frame(
    Outcome    = label,
    N          = nobs(model),
    Predictors = sum(!is.na(coef(model))) - 1,
    F          = unname(f[1]),
    df1        = unname(f[2]),
    df2        = unname(f[3]),
    p          = pf(f[1], f[2], f[3], lower.tail = FALSE),
    R2         = s$r.squared,
    Adj_R2     = s$adj.r.squared
  )
}

demo_models <- list(
  "WHO-5"             = m_WHO5_cross,
  "LoiTeS total"      = m_LoiTeS_full,
  "LoiTeS F1"         = m_LoiTeS_F1,
  "LoiTeS F2"         = m_LoiTeS_F2,
  "LoiTeS F3"         = m_LoiTeS_F3,
  "R-UCLA"            = m_Hughes,
  "OSTES total"       = m_Tschannen_total,
  "OSTES instruction" = m_Tschannen_instr,
  "OSTES class mgmt"  = m_Tschannen_mgmt,
  "OSTES engagement"  = m_Tschannen_eng,
  "MSPSS total"       = m_Zimet_total,
  "MSPSS sig. other"  = m_Zimet_sig,
  "MSPSS family"      = m_Zimet_fam,
  "MSPSS friends"     = m_Zimet_frd
)

omnibus_tab <- do.call(rbind, Map(omnibus_row, demo_models, names(demo_models)))
rownames(omnibus_tab) <- NULL
omnibus_tab$p_holm <- p.adjust(omnibus_tab$p, method = "holm")

kableExtra::kbl(omnibus_tab, digits = 3, booktabs = TRUE,
                caption = "Demographic regression models: omnibus tests and variance explained") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down", "striped"))

range(omnibus_tab$Adj_R2)   # adjusted R2 range for the text (all 14 models)
range(omnibus_tab$Predictors)

# ---- coefficient strings for the text ----------------------------
# e.g. report_coef(m_Hughes, "EmpStatusFreelance/Self employed")
report_coef <- function(model, term, digits = 2) {
  r <- robust_coefs(model)
  r <- r[r$Term == term, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) stop("Term not found. Available: ", paste(robust_coefs(model)$Term, collapse = "; "))
  sprintf(paste0("B = %.", digits, "f, 95%% CI [%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f], p %s"),
          r$B, r$CI_low, r$CI_high, fmt_p(r$p))
}

# ---- Table 2: hierarchical model, both blocks ----------------------
fmt_ci <- function(d) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", d$B, d$CI_low, d$CI_high)

b1 <- robust_coefs(m_h1)
b2 <- robust_coefs(m_h2)

hier_tab <- merge(
  data.frame(Term = b1$Term, `Block 1 B [95% CI]` = fmt_ci(b1),
             `p (1)` = fmt_p(b1$p), check.names = FALSE),
  data.frame(Term = b2$Term, `Block 2 B [95% CI]` = fmt_ci(b2),
             `p (2)` = fmt_p(b2$p), check.names = FALSE),
  by = "Term", all = TRUE, sort = FALSE
)

kableExtra::kbl(hier_tab, booktabs = TRUE, na = "",
                caption = "Hierarchical regression predicting LoiTeS total score (HC3 robust 95% CIs)") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down", "striped")) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general = "Reference groups are listed in the reference-group table. 1: R-UCLA + controls; 2 adds MSPSS, WHO-5 and OSTES.",
    general_title = "Note.", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| id: hier_influence

n_h2 <- nobs(m_h2)
cook <- cooks.distance(m_h2)
infl <- which(cook > 4 / n_h2)

cat("Cases with Cook's D > 4/N:", length(infl), "of", n_h2, "\n")

if (length(infl) > 0) {
  infl_tab <- data.frame(
    Row           = infl,
    Cooks_D       = cook[infl],
    Std_residual  = rstandard(m_h2)[infl],
    Leverage      = hatvalues(m_h2)[infl],
    row.names     = NULL
  )
  print(round(infl_tab, 3))
}

# Sensitivity analysis: do the conclusions change without Cook cases?
keep      <- setdiff(seq_len(n_h2), infl)
m_h2_trim <- lm(formula(m_h2), data = hier_df[keep, ])

sens <- merge(
  robust_coefs(m_h2)[,      c("Term", "B", "p")],
  robust_coefs(m_h2_trim)[, c("Term", "B", "p")],
  by = "Term", suffixes = c("_all", "_trimmed"), sort = FALSE
)

kableExtra::kbl(sens, digits = 3,
                caption = "Block 2 coefficients (HC3): all cases vs. excluding influential cases") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
```
